finding_and_required_action: Several flexural-stress formulas use shifting condition references (e.g., E19 checks B5, E20 checks B6, E21 checks B7) rather than a clearly fixed design-input cell. Trace each formula against the intended equation and correct references before relying on fatigue outputs.

The displayed total fatigue damage in B97 sums the left-hand BUC block only (H65+H80+H95). The right-hand TDC block is present in columns P:W; confirm whether separate TDC damage should be calculated and reported.

The workbook shows effective green time of 41 s and calculated phase greens around 18 s and 22 s (sum ≈39.6 s). Confirm lost time, all-red time, rounding, and whether the timing equations are consistently applied.
Growth rate is entered as 0.075 with a label indicating percent. Confirm this is intended to mean 7.5% per year and that the equation uses a decimal fraction consistently.

The workbook uses different denominators (65 kN and 80 kN) across the first data block, and 65 kN for both axle positions in the second block. Confirm reference standard / axle group basis for each formula.
Check whether axle proportions sum to 1.00 and clarify whether the lateral placement factor 0.25 is intended as a multiplier or percentage adjustment.
Add units, source references, design assumptions, version/date, and a legend distinguishing inputs from formula outputs. Correct spelling/labels where appropriate.

The four supplied workbooks do not provide clear calculations for superelevation, transition curves, sight distance, or horizontal/vertical alignment. Add the relevant workbook/field data if these items are to remain in the project title/scope.
